subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Wright Brothers' Wind Tunnel
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Wright Brothers' Wind Tunnel.

hook.text: The Wright brothers didn't just build a plane. They built a wind tunnel first — because the existing data was wrong.

buildup.text: Otto Lilienthal published lift tables that engineers trusted. The Wrights built a glider using those numbers. It barely flew.

discovery.text: They built a six-foot wind tunnel in their bicycle shop and tested over 200 wing shapes using a homemade balance.

twist.text: Lilienthal's data overestimated lift by 20%. The Wrights corrected the error and redesigned their wing from scratch.

climax.text: Their corrected aerodynamic data made the 1903 Kitty Hawk flight possible. Their wind tunnel was more important than the plane.

punchline.text: They didn't trust the data. They built their own. Then they flew.

quiz.question: Why did the Wright brothers build their own wind tunnel?
options: They wanted to test engine performance at different air speeds
Published lift data by Lilienthal was wrong, overestimating lift by 20%
No wind tunnels existed at the time and they invented the concept
